cases.answer: TAILORED-AF (multicenter RCT, 370 patients with drug-refractory persistent/long-standing persistent AF) reported that the tailored AI-guided ablation (targeting spatio-temporal dispersion areas plus PVI, n=187) took roughly twice as long as the anatomical PVI-only procedure (n=183): mean total procedure time 178±60 min vs 92±36 min, and total radiofrequency (RF) delivery time 42±17 min vs 20±11 min (both P<0.001; Table 2 also gives P<2.2×10⁻¹⁶). Initial mapping time was also longer (31±22 vs 10±5 min) and fluoroscopy time slightly longer (9±10 vs 5±4 min). The trade-off was that this additional procedural time bought superior efficacy — freedom from AF at 12 months after a single procedure was 88% in the tailored arm vs 70% in the anatomical arm (log-rank P<0.0001) — with no difference in the composite safety endpoint (death, cerebrovascular events, or treatment-related serious adverse events; 4% vs 3%, P>0.05).

claims.claim: Procedure and ablation times were twice as long in the tailored arm, with no difference in the safety endpoint.
